result.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
result.summary: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM? We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion injects the record's images, text and actions into the policy as a prefix and an action prior. Trained once on only 200 examples and deployed with a growing experience library, the model achieves state-of-the-art results on MolmoSpaces and RoboLab without any training on RoboLab: over native Cosmos 3 Nano, it raises success by 12.0 pp and 10.8 pp, reduces steps to success by 12.2% and 11.3%, and cuts regressions by 57%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 F$^3$，用 Form、Fit、Fusion 三步决定世界-动作模型如何利用自身经验：把成功与失败的 rollout 压缩为简短且经过验证的操作记录，训练策略读取记录并预测其何时有帮助，再将记录中的图像、文本与动作以前缀和动作先验形式注入策略，仅用 200 条样本训练并在增长的经验库上部署。
AI.relevance_reason: 「压缩经验记录 + 预测何时有用 + 前缀注入」的流程可能与 LVR 中视觉证据的筛选、进入推理状态的时机与接口问题相通，可供核查；但对象是机器人动作策略，尚无内部推理状态层面的证据。
